jobs.occupation: Qualified Massage Therapist Wanted – Full-Time or Part-Time
jobs.description:

We are seeking a therapist with solid practical experience in massage treatments, particularly sports massage and deep tissue massage.

Professional Qualifications

• 
Relevant professional education or certification in massage therapy.

• 
Proven practical experience in sports massage.

• 
Knowledge of human anatomy, muscles, and the musculoskeletal system is an advantage.

• 
Experience in other massage techniques, including oil massage and traditional Thai massage, is an advantage.

• 
Ability to assess clients' individual needs and provide appropriate treatments.

• 
Good communication skills in English or Danish.

Personal Qualifications

• 
Professional, reliable, and service-minded.

• 
Able to work independently and as part of an international team.

• 
Responsible, flexible, and committed to delivering high-quality treatments.

• 
Strong focus on customer satisfaction and professional service.

We Offer

• 
Full-time or part-time employment.

• 
A professional and international working environment.

• 
Formal employment contract and regulated working conditions.

• 
Salary, holiday entitlement, and pension arrangements in accordance with applicable Danish regulations and individual agreements.

Opportunities for professional development.

Employment Details

Workplace: Sunshine Thaimassage, Aaboulevard 3, 1ST, 1635 Copenhagen V, Denmark

Sunshine Thaimassage welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of nationality or background.

We look forward to hearing from you!

**

Are you commercially driven, curious about market needs and passionate about turning insights into successful products? We are looking for a Product Manager to take commercial ownership of our workwear assortment within the industry segment and help shape products that create real value for professional users.

Your role

As Product Manager, you will be the link between the market and our product development organization. You will translate customer needs, market insights and business strategy into competitive, relevant and profitable products for professionals working across industrial environments.

You will take responsibility for development projects from initial decision through to launch, working closely with Design, Product Development, Purchasing & Quality, Production, Marketing and Sales. Once products are launched, you will follow their commercial performance and use market feedback and data to continuously optimize the assortment.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Analysing market trends, customer needs, competitors and new developments within workwear and PPE for industrial environments

• Identifying product opportunities and assessing their market and commercial potential

• Defining product positioning, requirements, target pricing and expected profitability

• Preparing clear product briefs and driving development projects from concept to launch

• Working closely with Design and technical teams to ensure the right balance between functionality, durability, comfort, quality and market needs

• Coordinating cross-functional stakeholders throughout the development process to ensure progress and timely launches

• Building business cases and supporting commercial decisions for new products and collections

• Monitoring sales, profitability, assortment performance and market feedback and turning insights into concrete actions

• Driving continuous product improvements based on end-user feedback, quality data and sustainability considerations

• Developing and optimizing the industry assortment through product improvements, additions and phase-outs

• Providing clear product USPs and commercial input to Marketing and Sales

Who are you?

You combine a strong commercial mindset with an analytical and structured approach. You understand the needs of professional users and know how to translate market insights into relevant product opportunities. You are comfortable taking ownership and driving projects forward in collaboration with multiple stakeholders.

We expect that you:

• Have solid experience in product management and product development within technical textiles or apparel – ideally workwear

• Have experience with market and competitor analysis, benchmarking and product requirements

• Have successfully managed product development projects from concept to launch

• Have a good understanding of textile materials, functionality and technical product solutions

• Are commercially minded and comfortable working with pricing, margins and product performance

• Are structured, results-oriented and able to manage several projects simultaneously

• Communicate and collaborate effectively across functions and cultures

• Are fluent in English

You will join a highly cross-functional environment where market understanding, product expertise and commercial thinking come together to develop a competitive and relevant workwear assortment for professionals across the industrial sector.

What you can expect at our headquarters

Working at MASCOT is about more than the job itself. At our headquarters in Pårup, we want to create an environment where you can enjoy your working day, connect with colleagues and be part of an international organisation.

As part of the team, you can benefit from:

• On-site staff restaurant: daily freshly prepared meals available through our subsidised lunch scheme

• On-site gym: giving you the opportunity to stay active before or after work.

• Pension plan: providing additional security and helping you plan for the future

• Health insurance: giving you access to additional healthcare support when you need it

• An international working environment: collaborate with colleagues across different countries, functions and cultures

• Employee discounts: enjoy special discounts on MASCOT workwear and safety footwear

And most importantly, you will become part of a Danish family-owned company where collaboration, responsibility and long-term thinking are at the heart of how we work.

Ready to join us? We look forward to hearing from you.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate.

At MASCOT, we value diversity and equal opportunities. We are committed to creating an inclusive and respectful workplace. All applications are considered based on skills and qualifications, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, nationality, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other personal characteristic.

Help Create Structure and Alignment Across Our Supply Chain

Are you passionate about SIOP, data-driven decision-making, and building alignment across the supply chain?

Do you want to play a key role in building and driving our Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP) process while strengthening the connection between Sales, Production, Procurement, and Logistics?

At Etac, R82, we are looking for a SIOP Process Owner who can help take our planning and decision-making processes to the next level as part of our ambitious growth and transformation journey.

About the role

This is a newly established role that will play a significant part in how we plan, manage, and develop our supply chain going forward.

You will be responsible for establishing and driving our SIOP process, ensuring alignment between demand, inventory, capacity, and supply. At the same time, you will play a key role in transforming data into insights that support better and more proactive decision-making across the organization.

You will work closely with both the organization in Gedved and sales companies across our global Paediatrics business.

Initially, this is a specialist role reporting directly to the Head of Operations. Over time, we expect the function to evolve further and potentially include people management responsibilities.

You will join us at an exciting time as we continue to develop our Operations organization and implement our new ERP platform, M3.

Your key responsibilities

· Establish and continuously develop our SIOP process and ensure an effective planning and decision-making process across the organization

· Drive the monthly planning cycle across Sales, Production, Procurement, and Logistics

· Analyze forecast versus actual demand and translate insights into improvement initiatives and decision support

· Optimize inventory levels and support the balance between service levels and working capital

· Develop KPIs, dashboards, and management reporting

· Prepare scenarios and business impact analyses to support decision-making

· Contribute to the development of our data foundation and digital decision-support tools, including Power BI and future AI-enabled opportunities

· Ensure effective cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder alignment

What we are looking for

You do not need to tick every box from day one, but we imagine that you:

· Have experience within Supply Chain Planning, S&OP/SIOP, Operations, or Supply Chain Analytics

· Have worked with forecasting, inventory management, planning, or similar processes

· Hold a relevant educational background within Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field

· Have strong analytical skills and are comfortable working with large datasets

· Work in a structured manner and have a strong attention to detail

· Are able to translate data into actionable insights and improvements

· Thrive in a cross-functional environment with many stakeholders

· Communicate clearly and build strong relationships

· Are professionally proficient in English, both written and spoken. Danish is an advantage but not a requirement

It is an advantage if you:

· Have experience from an international company and collaborating with sales organizations globally

· Have experience working with ERP systems, preferably M3 or similar

· Have strong Excel skills and preferably experience with Power BI

· Have an interest in digital tools and emerging technologies

· Have experience building new processes, frameworks, or organizational structures

What we offer

We offer a central role with significant influence on the development of our future planning and decision-making processes. You will have the opportunity to build and shape a new function, work closely with the Operations leadership team, and create visible results across the organization.

Your daily work will combine analysis, business development, and operational execution, and you will become part of a highly collaborative environment where ambition, knowledge sharing, and teamwork go hand in hand.

Location: Gedved, Denmark

Questions?

If you would like to learn more about the position, please contact Claus Hjerrild, Head of Operations, Paediatrics EU & RoW, at +45 41 18 47 83.

Interested?

Please submit your CV, including a brief statement of motivation.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you.

About Etac

Etac is a world-leading developer of innovative assistive devices and patient handling equipment. Since 1973, we have been committed to improving quality of life for the individual, family members and caregivers.

Through our specialised product brands, we offer state-of-the-art solutions for a wide range of daily needs and care settings, for people at all stages of life. Headquartered in Sweden, Etac is a global company with around 1 500 employees, sales in over 80 countries and a revenue of approximately EUR 500 million.

We are looking for a Research Technician with a passion for research and innovation to join the Food Science Laboratory team at Arla Innovation Centre, Aarhus. If you enjoy hands-on laboratory work and have a strong interest in food science and physical analysis, this could be an opportunity for you.

The role will primarily support chemical analyses within the Food Science Laboratory. Candidates with relevant experience in physical analytical methods may have the opportunity to initially support physical analyses before transitioning into a chemistry-focused role. The balance between the two areas will vary over time according to business and project needs, providing an opportunity to develop expertise across multiple analytical disciplines.

This is a full-time fixed-term position until 31 December 2031.

About our team

We have a global role in Arla Research & Innovation (R&I) and our purpose is to transform food science into business opportunities for Arla. We drive food science-based research, partner up with product developers to create the future of dairy and support our production sites worldwide with ad hoc tasks. We are a team of scientists and technicians with vast experience in food science, and we are eager to find a new colleague to share our scientific passions with.

“In our team, we apply and develop a wide range of analytical methods to evaluate both the chemical composition and physical behaviour of our products. We use chromatographic and MS-based techniques to characterize aroma, protein, peptide, metabolite, carbohydrate and mineral profiles, alongside physical analyses such as particle and droplet size analysis, microstructure visualization, rheology, viscosity and functional characterization” says R&D Manager, Food Science Laboratory, Betina Mikkelsen

How you will make an impact

As a Research Technician you will be joining a department of 22 specialists, all experts within their fields. You will join a team of 11 technicians responsible for carrying out both physical and chemical analyses. Working closely with scientists and fellow technicians, you will contribute to a wide range of tasks and projects while having the flexibility to plan and prioritize your own work.

A typical task covers the following

• Taking in a request, coordinating and planning laboratory trials and analyses.

• Executing and reporting trials and analysis.

• Data handling, ordering the needed chemicals and maintaining our equipment.

• Our main chemistry analytical methods include GC-MS, LC-TOF, LC-QTOF and IC.

• Our main physical analytical methods include NMR, viscosity, light scattering methods, texture, stability test and advanced microscopy

• Data treatment is a big part of daily work.

What will make you successful

We expect that you have a degree as Laboratory Technician (in Danish “laborant”). Experience in chemical laboratory analyses is an advantage. Experience with physical analytical methods such as NMR, viscosity measurements, light scattering methods, texture analysis, stability testing or advanced microscopy is required for candidates who wish to start in our physical laboratory before transitioning into a chemistry-focused role.

Furthermore, it is essential that you

What do we offer?

This is a temporary full-time position until 31 December 2031. Position where you grow your analytical skills and learn every day. Our positive and collaborative culture will bring out the best in you. We have an international environment where knowledge sharing, and continuous learning are key words. Finally, we offer you a team that values open communication, good team spirit, passion for science, trust and respect.

Application and contact

We will review applications and invite for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible. For additional information, please call R&D Manager of Food Science Laboratory Betina Mikkelsen at +45 28253323

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Frontmatec is looking for a Cost & Value Engineer to play a key role in strengthening our cost and pricing capabilities across Meat Solutions Europe.

This position is critical to ensuring accurate cost calculations, competitive pricing, and profitable project execution. You will work closely with Product, Finance, Operations, Engineering, Sales, and Project Management, helping the business understand cost drivers and improve commercial decision-making.

What you'll do

• 
Develop and maintain cost calculation models for projects, equipment and solutions, by analyzing material, labor and manufacturing costs

• 
Drive transparency around cost structures and profitability.

• 
Support quotation and sales activities with accurate cost data.

• 
Identify cost-saving opportunities and cost optimization initiatives.

• 
Contribute to the continuous improvement of cost modelling processes and tools.

• 
Develop customer value analyses to support pricing decisions and demonstrate the commercial value of our solutions

• 
Identify, frame and drive value creation initiatives across projects and the existing product portfolio through quantitative analysis and cost modelling

• 
Facilitate cross-functional value engineering reviews with technical and commercial, translating improvement opportunities into actionable recommendations

What we're looking for

• 
3+ years of experience within cost structure, engineering, manufacturing, project business, finance, or a similar field.

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• 
Experience working with ERP systems and advanced Excel.

• 
Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and commercial stakeholders.

• 
Fluent in Danish and English.

This role offers a hybrid working environment. While many of your closest colleagues and stakeholders are based in Southern Denmark, you will collaborate with teams across our European organization.

Why join Frontmatec?

This is an opportunity to join a growing international organization where your work will have a direct impact on profitability, pricing strategies, and business performance. You'll become part of a collaborative environment in the Product Unit organization and work alongside experienced colleagues across Meat Solutions Europe.

If you enjoy combining technical understanding, business insight, and data-driven decision-making, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help us build the foundation for stronger commercial performance.

Project Director, Healthcare – Aarhus

Do you want to take ownership of one of the most strategic and visible programmes in Danish digital health? As Project Director, you will lead a comprehensive, product-strategic initiative for our electronic patient record (EPR) product, which has the potential to become the foundation for international growth. Sounds exciting? Then seize the chance now!

Systematic Healthcare – a coherent healthcare system

Systematics’ healthcare solutions are used by more than 200,000 users in, among others, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, the UK and New Zealand. Our EPR solution is the core system in a hospital and has been developed in close collaboration with our customers.

Experienced Project Director with ownership, impact and business understanding

As Project Director, you will have overall responsibility for one of Systematics’ most strategic initiatives: an extensive, long-term, product-strategic programme for our EPR product. The programme is closely linked to the EPR solution used in Western Denmark today and is characterised by high complexity, both internally and externally, with many stakeholders including our customers.

The role is not only about delivering on time, price, scope and quality - as our new Project Director, you help create the framework for the program and ensure that both our customers and Systematic realise the expected benefits.

You are the programme’s single point of accountability towards both the steering committee, our customers management and the management in Systematic.

The programme is run as a virtual organisation across tracks such as development, product management, customer projects, implementation and operations. You have no direct reports and therefore create results through influence, trust, clear direction and strong governance. You report to the Vice President for the area and work closely with our customers, Product Management and the leadership of the EPR area.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Owning the programme plan, budget and business case, and ensuring a coherent solution and the expected benefits over the programme’s lifetime.

• Establishing and driving the programme’s governance and acting as the programme’s primary representative towards customer and Systematic management, including preparing and presenting decision papers.

• Actively owning and protecting the scope: challenging new requirements, driving priorities and ensuring an effective change management process.

• Owning the roadmap, schedule, milestones, budget and resource plan, and ensuring proactive risk management with timely escalation to the steering committee.

• Ensuring delivery in accordance with the agreements and leading changes and negotiations together with our Sales and Legal teams and the Vice President.

• Managing a complex stakeholder landscape, internally and externally, including customers and their regional top management, political decision-makers, clinical leadership, partners and internal units, and ensuring that the product roadmap is aligned with the programme’s commitments.

• Building and leading the virtual programme organisation across tracks and departments by setting direction, removing obstacles and being an ambassador for culture and collaboration. At the same time, you support the organisational change that the programme entails

You will be based at our office in Aarhus and can expect customer meetings around Denmark. Your success is measured by whether the programme delivers within the agreed time, price, scope and quality, and whether the benefits of the business case are realised. An important success criterion is the trust of customers and management in the programme.

Your competencies and qualifications

We envision that you have 10–15 years of experience in programme and project management, several of them with large, complex IT programmes of similar complexity: multi-year, with several parallel tracks, many stakeholders and organisational interfaces. You hold a master’s degree, for example in engineering, IT or economics, and ideally a certification in programme management, such as PMI PgMP or Axelos MSP.

In addition, we expect that you:

• Have experience from the IT industry and with public customers, large public contracts and politically governed organisations. Experience from the healthcare sector is a significant advantage.

• Have been responsible for budget, business case and contractual commitments, including negotiating changes with customers.

• Have experience reporting to executive management and steering committees, leading in matrix or virtual organisations without formal line authority, and taking part in organisational change.

• Have a strong understanding of business and finance, as well as experience in contract and risk management.

• Speak Danish as your native language and are fluent in English.

As a person, you:

Take ownership: You act as the owner of the programme, not as an administrator of plans and reports, and you have the courage to say no and make difficult prioritisations.

Lead through influence: You create commitment and results without formal authority.

Have executive presence and political awareness: You are credible at executive level and communicate complex topics clearly and in a balanced way.

Are commercial and customer-minded: You balance customer value with Systematic’s interests and understand the importance of our customers’ work for patients and clinicians.

Are structured, proactive and resilient: You create overview, make decisions on an incomplete basis, and keep your energy and calm throughout a long, high-paced programme.

Are demanding and inclusive: You create an open and honest environment where people are heard and their work is recognised.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Architect the services behind mission-critical C4I capabilities. You'll shape how we turn a robust, commercial-off-the-shelf product into real operational value – acting as a trusted advisor across our international service delivery teams

The job

As Senior Solution Architect, you'll help customers achieve their desired outcomes through standardised service offerings. You'll drive the implementation of our service development strategy and business model, ensuring both commercial success and customer value.

Leveraging our products and global best practices, you'll develop solutions that enhance customer capabilities across their organisations, processes, technology and competences. You'll act as a trusted advisor and key enabler across our service delivery teams, inspiring and supporting local teams as they guide customers to strengthen their capabilities and realise the value of our solutions.

Your key responsibilities:

• Designing service offerings for C4I capabilities that drive customer value and operational effectiveness

• Leading the development of our service catalogue from a technical perspective

• Advising customers on designing and deploying our systems, and defining business and technical requirements together with them

• Creating and maintaining roadmap items that guide the evolution and commercial success of our service offerings

• Advising and inspiring our global constellations to ensure consistent, high-quality service delivery across customer engagements

You'll also help adapt military delivery models and standards, develop service descriptions and supporting materials, and contribute to both pre-sales and post-sales activities.

For this role, you should expect occasional business travel of 10-40 days a year, typically in short trips lasting 2-4 days.

Joining the team

You'll report to Marie Lunde Jørgensen, Manager Defence Service Development and work out of our head office in Aarhus or Copenhagen, Denmark. The team brings together expertise in product portfolio management, solution architecture, military domain knowledge, system engineering and business analytics.

The team works strategically to define service concepts, develop business models and shape offerings in close collaboration with global stakeholders across Systematic, while also engaging broadly across the organisation to ensure alignment and drive success.

Your qualifications

• At least 5 years of experience as a Solution Architect within IT systems, product development and bespoke integrations

• A relevant technical bachelor's or master's degree

• Strong expertise in deploying large-scale, complex IT solutions, including cloud, containers and on-premises infrastructure

• Sound understanding of microservices and enterprise architecture principles

• Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with a talent for advising and influencing with impact

• A structured, detail-oriented and proactive approach to problem-solving in dynamic environments

• Experience in technical or end-user training to support effective knowledge transfer

It would also be an advantage if you bring:

• Familiarity with military IT systems, networks or architecture frameworks, such as NAF, DoDAF or TOGAF

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

About the job

As our Portfolio Intelligence & Analytics Manager you will build and maintain a structured portfolio intelligence capability that identifies, evaluates, and prioritizes external growth opportunities across European markets.

In this role, you will translate market intelligence, competitive insights, and analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for Business Development, Portfolio Management, and senior stakeholders.

• Apply analytics, automation, AI, and digital tools to improve the scalability and quality of the portfolio intelligence capability

• Support broader Business Intelligence activities, including dashboards, reporting, forecasting, and ad hoc analyses

This role requires on-site presence at our headquarters in Odense twice a week.

Who are you?

We are looking for a commercially minded professional with demonstrated expertise in market intelligence and a strong track record of turning complex data into actionable business insights. Experience in the pharmaceutical industry is a significant advantage, particularly within Portfolio Support, Generics, Business Development, Portfolio Management, Market Intelligence, or pharmaceutical consulting. You hold a master’s degree in Business Analytics, Economics, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Life Sciences, or a related field.

You know how to connect analytical findings with portfolio priorities and growth opportunities. You can assess markets, competitors, pipelines, strategic fit, risks, and commercial potential, then communicate your conclusions through compelling data visualizations and decision-ready presentations.

• A curious, proactive mindset and a strong motivation to solve business problems through data

Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

• Experience with or a strong interest in Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), with Twilio Segment experience considered a plus.

• Proven ability to perform tracking audits, quality assurance, and debugging, identifying and resolving challenges related to event tracking, attribution, CORS, CSP, and data collection.

Working at DFDS At DFDS, you will be part of an environment where technology, collaboration, and business impact go hand in hand. This role offers the opportunity to work on meaningful digital initiatives that influence how we engage with customers across channels and platforms.

• Meaningful scope: Help shape the Martech and customer data foundation behind important digital journeys.

• Modern collaboration: Work closely with colleagues across engineering, analytics and marketing.

• Growth opportunities: Develop your skills in frontend engineering, customer platforms, data flows, and personalisation.

While you’re with us, we want you to develop. At DFDS, we believe that development happens first and foremost through activities in the workplace. We will also offer training courses that can support you in your role, if needed.

Are we a match? Then what are you waiting for? Apply Now. If you think your personality, skills, experience, and desire match this role, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your CV as soon as possible, as we’re keen to meet potential candidates on an ongoing basis.

For questions regarding the technical scope or team culture, feel free to reach out to Frontend Chapter Lead, Noman Ahmed Khan at nkhan@dfds.com. Please note that we only consider applications submitted directly through our official recruitment system.

We look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools 	
• Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position 	
• Relevant educational background 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Good written and oral English language skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; 	
• Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications; 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; 	
• Publication list (if available); 	
• Names and contact details of three references.    

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is November 22, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment.

  The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk  

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.
